transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-06 15:00 PT | Duration approx 55m | Recording flagged
Attendees: Alex Park (Redwood AE), Morgan Lee (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (Redwood CSM), Luis Navarro (Redwood SRE), Devon Tran (Product); Sana Patel (Helio Head of ML), Jorge Ruiz (Helio Infra), Becky Tanner (Helio Finance), Tomoko Saito (Helio Security), Caleb Moore (Helio PM)

-- Auto-summary (auto generated, may be partial) --
Priya: quick pulse - usage rising, cost concerns; Sana: wants pilot faster; Becky: needs PO threshold; Tomoko: needs KMS + SOC2 confirmation; Morgan: proposes perf runs + KV cache tuning; Alex: pilot SOW proposal and pricing tiers.

[00:00] Alex (AE): hey everyone, thanks for carving time. quick agenda — recap pilot ask, run through economics, security blockers, and then bench plan. if anything missing call it out.
[00:28] Sana (Helio): thanks Alex, yeah we want to accelerate this pilot — our lighthouse feature is blocking on latencies for long form generation, and finance is pressing on burn.
[01:05] Becky (Finance): hi — short intro — we need clarity on committed spend vs variable, and what safe guards exist so we don't overshoot in week 1.
[01:22] Alex: totally. i'll outline two options: hosted credit-backed pilot (fast onboarding) or dedicated reserved pool for predictable throughput. both have burst/overage behaviors.
[01:45] Morgan (SE): quick piece — for Helio's workload (long form, 1.5k tokens typical) we recommend continuous batching with prefix caching and a quantized model to hit target latencies. we'll share perf numbers.
[02:12] Jorge (Infra): can you remind us what the KV cache behavior is with warm starts? we saw big token cost on replays during our PoC last month.
[02:31] Morgan: yes so Redwood's runtime will do automatic prefix/KV caching; on warm starts the KV hits should reduce per-token compute, but initial cold sequences still cost. also key point — cache is sticky per model variant and per customer routing key, so warmup window matters.
[03:10] Caleb (PM): what's the recommended warmup duration? we've seen 48 hours mentioned.
[03:21] Luis (Redwood SRE): depends on traffic, but for Helio's cadence i'd budget 10k tokens/sec sustained for 48-72 hours to reach good cache hit rates. that roughly maps to our suggested 2-week warmup to be safe for production SLOs.
[04:00] Becky: two weeks warmup — ok but that's more spend. do you have staged pricing?
[04:18] Alex: yes — propose 2-week warmup discounted at 30% off hosted list, then pilot weeks 3-6 have tiered commits with burst credits and a cap you set. we'll share the SOW numbers after this call.
[04:45] Becky: can we put a hard monthly cap during pilot? procurement may need that.
[04:53] Alex: yes we can — cap + alerts + programmatic throttling. we'll include a kill-switch and alerts to notify both sides at thresholds.
[05:12] Tomoko (Security): on security — we need to validate data residency, KMS integration, key custody, and SOC2 evidence. is Redwood Private required or can hosted suffice with our DPA?
[05:34] Alex: hosted can work for many customers with our standard DPA and region pins, but for KMS/HSM and customer-managed keys we recommend Private deployment or at minimum Dedicated with VPC peering and KMIP/HSM integration.
[06:05] Tomoko: our legal eats through DPA quickly but keys are the blocker — we cannot have raw PII leaving our KMS policy.
[06:22] Luis (Redwood SRE): we support cloud KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS), and for enterprise we can do HSM-backed key material on Private. we'll share the integration diagram and SOC2 artifacts.
[06:45] Tomoko: also audit logs granularity? we need per-request metadata for compliance.
[06:58] Morgan: Redwood Console exposes token-level cost and per-route traces; we can push logs to your SIEM. some field names might be redacted but we can provide request IDs and model variant traces.
[07:25] Sana: excellent — that helps. on the performance side — our target p95 generation latency is sub-1.8s for 1.5k token prompts, is that realistic?
[07:40] Morgan: with a quantized medium-latency model and dedicated A100-ish nodes, yes — but hosted multi-tenant runs slightly higher variability. dedicated gives tighter SLOs.
[08:05] Jorge: what about cost delta — dedicated vs hosted? rough order of magnitude?
[08:15] Alex: rough ballpark: hosted is pay-per-use and can be 25-40% cheaper at low utilization, but dedicated with reserved commits becomes cheaper beyond ~60% util. depends on your workload shape.
[08:50] Becky: can you show a scenario — we have seasonal spikes and a baseline of steady 10 qps.
[09:03] Devon (Product): i'll stop you — Morgan, can you sketch a quick scenario of warmup + burst?
[09:12] Morgan: sure: baseline 10qps with median 1.2k tokens; with prefix caching expected per-token compute drops by ~18% after warmup. bursts to 60qps for short windows need burst capacity — we advise a hybrid reserved baseline with spare burst credits.
[09:40] Alex: action item — we'll model three scenarios in the benchmark sheet and include a variant with caching disabled to show worst-case.
[09:50] Sana: sounds good. procurement — Becky, timeline?
[09:57] Becky: internal approval needs a PO signoff; threshold for auto-approve is $150k. if pilot is under that with clear capped burn we can move fast.
[10:10] Alex: ok we'll target pilot pricing under that cap; if not we will split billing cadence or stage pilots.

[10:45] -- Perf deep dive & bench notes --
[10:46] Morgan: technical note — we'll do a perf run on your models and our recommended quantization pathway. we use continuous batching and kernel selection optimizations; sometimes memory layout differences lead to 5-10% var.
[11:18] Jorge: are you able to run on-prem GPUs? we have some spare V100s but prefer cloud.
[11:27] Morgan: Redwood Private supports on-prem but kernel parity varies; A100/80gb and later give best perf. V100 will work but expect slower KV throughput.
[11:45] Caleb: any chance to test with our real model weights?
[11:52] Morgan: yes we can spin a bench with a customer-supplied model bundle under an NDA - need to confirm licensing.
[12:10] Tomoko: NDA is fine, but then we need to hash verify artifact movement and wipe steps.
[12:22] Priya (CSM): we'll coordinate legal and repo access — Priya to own logistics.

[13:00] Becky: circling back to burn — can we get per-route alerts and an automated throttle at 80% of budget?
[13:12] Luis (Redwood SRE): yes, Redwood Console supports route-level quotas and alerting hooks; we can set programmatic throttles to degrade to a smaller model variant at 80/90%.
[13:35] Becky: degrade is ok as long as fallback quality is acceptable.
[13:42] Devon: we can run side-by-side evals with your prompt set to map quality drop vs cost savings.

[14:05] Sana: timeline request — we'd like pilot started by Jan 4 2027. realistic?
[14:18] Alex: yes, provided legal and procurement windows align. we need signatures + infra checklist ~2 weeks prior for dedicated/private. for hosted could be less than 72 hours.
[14:37] Becky: so timeline looks doable if we get SOW this week.
[14:45] Alex: we'll deliver SOW and pilot SOW and pricing matrices by 2026-12-08.

[15:10] -- Security specifics --
[15:11] Tomoko: a few specifics — are request logs encrypted at rest, do you support customer-managed keys for the logs, and can we push logs to our SIEM without PII?
[15:28] Luis: logs encrypted at rest; for Private you can keep keys in your HSM. we can redact PII fields before shipping logs and provide structured request metadata.
[15:50] Tomoko: great. also looking for an attestation of SOC2 controls mapped to our controls matrix — can you provide that?
[15:59] Alex: yes — we'll provide SOC2 Type II report and a controls mapping doc.

[16:20] -- Procurement discussion --
[16:21] Becky: to help approval i'll need a one-page exec summary: pilot goal, max cap, expected outcome, and renewal options.
[16:28] Alex: we'll produce that; Alex to own exec summary and send with SOW.

[17:00] -- Recap & agreements --
[17:01] Priya: quick recap — agreed pilot: 6 weeks total, 2-week warmup + 4-week validation. committed baseline with burst credits. cap and throttles in place. security deep-dive scheduled. performance bench to run with your model weights under NDA. deliverables: SOW, pricing, bench plan, SOC2 artifacts.
[17:34] Sana: yes that's accurate. thank you.
[17:42] Alex: next meeting — security deep-dive w/ Tomoko & Luis — propose week of 2026-12-13, is that ok?
[17:50] Tomoko: yes, mornings PST best.
[17:55] Becky: i'll try to clear PO gate by 2026-12-11.

[18:10] Alex: thanks all. we'll follow up with docs + sheet. end.
